chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Abū Ismāʿīl al-Sarrāj, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān, from Qudāmah ibn Abī Zayd al-Ḥammār, from some of our companions, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him: What is the minimum distance that should be between a water well and a cesspit? He said: “If the land is soft, then seven cubits; and if it is mountainous, then five cubits.”

Then he said: “Water flows toward the qiblah to the right, and it flows from the right of the qiblah to the left of the qiblah, and it flows from the left of the qiblah to the right of the qiblah, and it does not flow from the qiblah toward the rear of the qiblah.”

key_terms.يَجْرِي الْمَاءُ: the movement or flow of water

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum distance between a water well and a cesspit in Shi'i fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the minimum distance between a water well and a cesspit, distinguishing between soft land and mountainous ground. It also describes the directional flow of water in relation to the qiblah, which serves as part of determining practical rulings concerning water and purity.
